title: Spread a wet-floor sign to its hinge stop with both hands and stand it at the spill
instruction: Open the folded wet-floor sign all the way and leave it standing by itself at the near edge of the spill, square to it and not on it.
context: Janitors and building cleaners (O*NET 37-2011.00; 2,432,600 US jobs in 2025, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook) "Clean spills and other hazards with appropriate equipment" (BLS duties). The first piece of that equipment is the wet-floor sign, set out open at the spill before the mop. The hard parts, in order. (1) Nothing holds the sign down: pull one leaf and the whole sign slides toward the hand (on the GPU one hand alone opened it only 9 degrees and dragged the other foot 22 to 25 mm, scoring 0.25), so each hand draws its own leaf outward and the two pulls cancel. (2) Both draws follow arcs about the hinge 610 mm up and must stay equal until the hinge reaches its stop; short of it the base is narrow and the sign tips. (3) Equal draws open it in place, beside the spill and off it. (4) Both hands let go and lift clear without knocking it.
setup: Bimanual YAM station. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm; the table top is z 0 and stands for a corridor's smooth floor; the corridor runs along y. Three objects. (1) A two-leaf A-frame wet-floor sign modelled on the Rubbermaid Commercial FG611277YEL two-sided Caution Wet Floor sign (listed 11 x 12 x 25 in, 1.95 lb shipping weight, about 15 USD, WebstaurantStore item 690611277YEL; its top carry handle is not modelled), yellow, 0.55 kg in all (est), standing folded: leaves face to face, its ridge (the top hinge) along x, 610 mm up, its middle at x 330 mm, y +10 mm; leaf A faces -y (the right arm), leaf B faces +y (the left arm). Each leaf is a 12 mm thick sheet 280 mm wide (along x) and 610 mm tall, 0.275 kg, with a black rubber foot pad 30 mm deep, 260 mm wide and 8 mm thick along its inner bottom edge, a printed warning on its outer face (pictogram and CAUTION WET FLOOR; in the simulation a black panel 200 x 150 mm centred 440 mm up) and a pull handle fitted low on its outer face for the gripper (not on the stock sign): a solid yellow fin 20 mm across (along x) standing 140 mm out from the face, from 30 to 120 mm up, centred across the leaf. The hinge (friction 0.02 N m, est) opens to a moulded stop at 25 degrees between the leaves (each 12.5 degrees off vertical), the feet then 264 mm apart. Pad friction 0.6 (est). (2) A fixed spill patch: a flat blue mat 300 x 200 x 1 mm, its 300 mm edge along x, x 200 to 500 mm, y 232 to 432 mm. (3) The corridor's side wall: a plain beige block 40 mm thick and 300 mm high at x 600 to 640 mm, y -600 to +600 mm. Nothing else is on the table. Opened in place about its hinge line, the sign's +y foot ends 90 mm from the patch's near edge; folded, its +y grab handle ends 70 mm from it.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the sign's pose and both grippers. Open: the two foot lines 244 to 270 mm apart (the stop gives 264 mm; 244 mm is 1.9 degrees of hinge short of it). Lean: each leaf 9 to 16 degrees from vertical. Placed: the nearer foot line 40 to 140 mm from the patch's near edge (along y) and neither foot pad over the patch (each pad, top view). Beside: the hinge's middle within the patch's 300 mm length (x 200 to 500 mm). Square: the ridge within 10 degrees of the patch's long edge. Stands: both foot lines within 10 mm of the table top, and over the last 2 s no foot line or the hinge moves more than 3 mm, the spread changes under 2 mm and no leaf turns more than 1 degree. Hands off: on every step of the last 2 s both grippers' finger zones are 50 mm or more from every part of the sign. Score 0 if the sign's state is unreadable, either leaf ends more than 45 degrees from vertical, the sign does not stand, or the spread is under 70 mm (do nothing scores 0). Otherwise: 1.0 open, lean, placed, beside, square, stands and hands off; 0.75 the same but a gripper within 50 mm; 0.5 stands and open, ridge within 30 degrees, no pad over the patch, but a leaf outside its lean window, placement outside its band, not beside, or ridge 10 to 30 degrees off; 0.25 stands with the spread at least 70 mm otherwise (not open to the stop, ridge over 30 degrees off, or a pad over the patch). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held 1 s. Real trial, per condition: open, a tape between the foot lines; lean, a digital inclinometer on each leaf; placed, a rule from the foot line to the patch edge and a look from above; beside, a tape along the patch edge to below the ridge's middle; square, a 10 degree protractor against the patch edge; stands, a spacer under each foot, 2 s by the clock and a mark at each foot (3 mm gauge); hands off, a 50 mm spacer block against each hand; zero gate, an inclinometer at 45 degrees.
fidelity: Rigid leaves on a revolute hinge with a hard stop at 25 degrees (no detent), not flexing moulded plastic. Each leaf carries a 140 mm pull fin low on its face that the stock FG611277YEL lacks: a robot adaptation so the top-down wrist (about 52 mm) clears the 610 mm leaf. Mass 0.55 kg (the stock sign ships at 1.95 lb), pad friction 0.6, hinge friction 0.02 N m are estimates. The print is a black panel; the table is the floor. Carrying the sign to the spill is not modelled.
reset_notes: Fold the sign and stand it with its ridge along x, its middle at x 330 mm, y +10 mm, leaf A facing -y. Lay the patch at x 200 to 500 mm, y 232 to 432 mm. Nothing is consumed. Check the hinge swings freely to its stop and the pads are clean and dry.
